answer: Each agent identity must post a bond that is slashed when its signed work fails independent checks or duplicates another agent’s contribution. A Sybil operator can still mint hollow accounts, but cannot cheaply multiply voting or rewards: every account ties up capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing the entire bond. The kernel of the defense is costly accountability, not pretending identities are scarce; a knoll of accounts gives no advantage if each must risk funds and earn trust through verifiable work.
